definitions.gloss: sweat gland — the gland in the skin that produces perspiration
definitions.explanation: One of the glands in the skin that secretes sweat. Humans have two main types: {エクリン汗腺|かんせん} (eccrine sweat glands), distributed over most of the body and important for temperature regulation, and {アポクリン汗腺|かんせん} (apocrine sweat glands), found mainly in the armpits and groin and linked to body odor.

examples.english: Sweat comes out from the sweat glands.

examples.english: Exercise activates the sweat glands, improving the body's ability to regulate its temperature.

notes:
Compound of {汗|かん} ('sweat') and ⟦{腺|せん}→腺：17997_sen⟧ ('gland'). Has several homophones including ⟦{幹線|かんせん}→幹線：15069_kansen⟧ ('trunk line'), ⟦{感染|かんせん}→感染：05977_kansen⟧ ('infection'), and ⟦{観戦|かんせん}→観戦：14142_kansen⟧ ('watching a match').

USAGE:
- Medical and biological term; used in health articles, textbooks, and discussions of skin care, thermoregulation, and body odor.
- Commonly specified with type prefixes: エクリン{汗腺|かんせん} (eccrine) and アポクリン{汗腺|かんせん} (apocrine).
- Related everyday concepts include ⟦{発汗|はっかん}→発汗：13705_hakkan⟧ ('sweating/perspiration') and {体温調節|たいおんちょうせつ} ('body-temperature regulation').
